meta.title: Research Overview
meta.subtitle: Radiation loss engineering of $\pi$ shift Bragg grating cavities
meta.author: Evyatar Rubin

frames.title: Main conclusions
items: Apodization and tooth shift trade loss against mode length.
Structures beside the cavity reduce loss and leave the mode length unchanged.
TM radiates in the propagation plane, so an air trench or a SiN cylinder row \textcolor{green!50!black}{reduces its loss}. TE does not.
At fixed width, inverse design \textcolor{green!50!black}{does better than any of the hand tuned levers}, though it is still below the lab's overshoot.
Reflectors, scatterers and SiO$_2$ cylinders inside the core \textcolor{red!75!black}{do not help}.

frames.title: What worked
frames.note: All the levers reduce loss; apodization is the only one that lengthens the mode.

frames.title: What did not work
rows: SiO$_2$ or air holes in core
frames.note: Holes in the core radiate and kill the resonance. Everything else here either adds loss of its own or never reaches the leaky lobe.

frames.title: $Q$ factor at a 20\,$\mu$m mode and a -3\,dB peak
frames.caption: Each device lengthened until its peak is -3\,dB at a 20\,$\mu$m mode. Lateral structures give about a third more $Q$, inverse design about 6×; the TE overshoot bar is projected.

frames.heading: Details
frames.subheading: TE, TE versus TM, TM levers, inverse design

frames.title: TE: apodization reduces loss and widens the mode
items: Linear apodization: loss reduced, mode much wider.
Tanh gives the same gain with less widening.

items.text: A few apodized periods are enough; more add nothing.
items.detail: The lab's overshoot apodization is far stronger, and only its amplitude sets the mode length.

frames.title: TE: shifting the innermost teeth recycles the leak

items.text: Shifting the innermost teeth outward reduces loss with the mode length unchanged.
items.detail: Light that would leak at the cavity is redirected into the mode; the far field collapses to one lobe.

items: A two tooth particle swarm design gave the best transmission per width.
\textbf{In fabrication:} devices matched the same optimum, with slightly stronger coupling.

blocks.label: At the same length
blocks.text: TM couples more weakly, so lower loss, lower $Q$, wider mode.

blocks.label: At the same peak transmission
blocks.text: TM is longer and its $Q$ is about three times higher.

blocks.label: At the operating point
blocks.text: The plain gratings tie. TM radiates in the propagation plane, TE upward.

frames.title: TM: the teeth behave as in TE, but the shift works differently
items: Apodization reduces loss, widens the mode, and saturates.
A large shift of the innermost teeth widens the mode and shows no optimum; TM does not recycle at the cavity.
Once apodization saturates, small shifts on many teeth \textcolor{green!50!black}{add further gain at fixed width}; the inverse design uses this.

frames.title: TM: a trench reduces loss, a third more $Q$ at the benchmark
frames.caption: The trench returns the in plane radiation by total internal reflection; the mode length is unchanged. A trench stopping at the core top keeps most of the gain in one lithography step.

frames.title: TM: a row of SiN cylinders does the same, one lithography step
items: The row is a weak grating: its period sets the beam angle, $n_\text{clad}\,\sin\theta = n_\text{eff} - \lambda/\Lambda$.
Aimed at the radiation lobe, sliding the row sets the phase: one phase cancels the lobe, the opposite grows it.
A second row on the other side adds a few percent; a third adds nothing.

frames.title: Inverse design: what is optimized

items.text: 3D adjoint optimization of the 25 innermost teeth per side (depth, width, shift), the cavity width and the cylinder row, TM.
detail: \textbf{Constraints}\; the mode length and the resonance wavelength are held fixed.

items: Width penalties and second moment proxies failed; projecting each gradient step onto both constraints works.

frames.title: Inverse design: what it found so far
items: Transmission rises steadily with the resonance and the mode length held.
The design is a gentle rise in corrugation toward the arms, a mild overshoot.

items.text: The cylinder row does not move when freed: its optimum is separable and set analytically.
items.detail: About 6× the plain grating at the operating point, still below the lab's TE overshoot.

frames.title: Next steps
items: \textbf{Restart} the inverse design with more free teeth.
\textbf{Adapt} the overshoot apodization model to TM and use it as the starting point.
\textbf{Open a TE lane} seeded from the overshoot profile, where the larger gains are.
